bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Three-part stated framework: "Prioritize businesses", "Streamline the portfolio" and "Allocate capital to portfolio priorities" — described as "Focused businesses, Selective capital allocation for superior value creation".
- Capex of Rs 300-350 crore per year is to be "funded through internal accruals", with the majority of growth capex directed to "high-margin, high ROCE businesses".
- Capital release lever is working capital: average NWC days cut from 54 in Q1FY25 to 21 in Q1FY27, framed as "NET WORKING CAPITAL EFFICIENCY IMPROVED SHARPLY, DRIVING HEALTHY ROCE".
- Exit/closure discipline forms part of the allocation stance (strategic review of e.g. Shrimp Feed, plant closures evaluated, sub-scale sub-segment exits, Live Bird Trading closure).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Scale leadership in two core categories - described as the 'Largest Feed Player in India with 30+ Manufacturing Plants' and the 'Largest Crude Palm Oil Producer in India', with 60+ pan-India manufacturing units across businesses
- Diversified agri portfolio across Animal Nutrition, Crop Care, Oil Palm, Dairy and Foods - management attributes FY 2025-26 results to 'the strength of our diversified portfolio', with a standout Oil Palm year offsetting a weak Crop Care environment
- Farmer-engagement distribution moat - deep on-ground outreach, field-level demonstrations and an Oil Palm Samadhan centre network expanded to 24 centres (10 added in FY 2025-26, 5 of them in the North East); 20,000+ farmers supported through CSR initiatives
- Brand equity in Animal Nutrition - repeatedly cited 'strong brand equity' plus the established Bypro franchise and the Dhanalaxmi cattle-feed line, supporting volume-led growth and premium launches
- Dedicated R&D infrastructure across segments - NGCARD (Nashik) for cattle/broiler/layer feed, the Aqua Feed R&D Centre (Hanuman Junction), the Adi Godrej Centre for Chemical Research & Development (Rabale), plus oil palm R&D; enables customised nutrition products, molecule development in Crop Care/Astec and yield improvements in Oil Palm
- Vertically integrated oil palm model - plantation development, nursery operations, FFB procurement, milling with improving oil extraction ratio, and downstream optimisation, giving upstream-to-downstream operating leverage on a maturing asset base
- Improving capital efficiency and balance-sheet quality - ROCE improved from 16% in FY 2024-25 to 20% in FY 2025-26 and average working capital days cut from 39 to 25; ICRA long-term rating of AA (Stable)
- Scale milestone and track record - crossed the milestone of Rs 10,000 Crore in consolidated revenues for the first time in FY 2025-26, with a stated 10-year revenue CAGR of 11%
- Astec's chemistry and CDMO capability - state-of-the-art Adi Godrej Centre for Chemical Research and Development, diversified chemistry capabilities and a sharpened business-development focus, exporting to approximately 17 countries
- Governance and group heritage - part of the more than century-old Godrej Group; Board of 12 directors with half independent and 6 women directors (4 of them independent)
- Sustainability credentials that are ahead of sector norms - CDP 'A-' leadership band for Climate and Forests for a second consecutive year, water-positive status at ~14x conservation, 78% renewable energy share, and approved science-based emission targets aligned to 'Well Below 2 degrees C'
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Climate change and increasing weather volatility — Flagged as a key long-term risk for agri-linked businesses. Increasing frequency of unseasonal rainfall, heat stress, droughts, floods and shifting monsoon patterns can materially impact crop acreage, animal productivity, feed availability and demand cycles, affecting volumes, raw material availability, cost structures and farmer purchasing behaviour across multiple verticals. Already realised in FY 2025-26 — unseasonal rain during Q1 disrupted Dairy demand patterns.
- Geo-political developments and supply chain disruption — Global geo-political tensions, trade disruptions and regional instability pose risks of supply chain interruptions, increased freight costs, commodity price volatility, foreign exchange fluctuations and constrained availability of key inputs such as grains, oilseeds, energy and agrochemical raw materials. The Company diversifies sourcing and optimises inventories, but prolonged disruptions could impact input costs and margins.
- Raw material availability, price volatility and supplier dependency — Businesses depend on availability of quality raw materials at competitive prices. Prices of maize, soya, oilcakes, milk, energy, packaging materials and chemical intermediates are volatile, driven by weather, global demand-supply, currency, trade policies and regulatory changes. Dependence on third-party suppliers and logistics partners adds exposure to supply disruptions, cost escalation and delivery delays.
- Regulatory, policy and compliance risk across agri, food and agrochemicals — Sectors are subject to evolving oversight on product approvals, pricing controls, environmental norms, sustainability disclosures, product safety, labelling and quality standards. Changes in frameworks, approval delays or restrictive policy actions may impact product launches, cost structures and business continuity; rising ESG expectations require continuous investment in compliance, sustainability and reporting systems.
- Capital allocation, execution and people risk in a diversified multi-vertical structure — Managing diversified operations across multiple geographies and business verticals requires strong execution discipline, leadership depth and robust internal controls. Risks around talent availability, succession planning, digital capability absorption, project execution and integration of new initiatives may impact long-term value creation if not managed effectively. Leadership transition was live during the year — the Managing Director superannuated with effect from close of business on August 31, 2025, with a CEO & Managing Director appointed to the Managing Committee from September 1, 2025.
- Milk procurement cost inflation and competitive intensity in the Dairy business — The Dairy business faced a significantly challenging operating environment in FY 2025-26; sustained inflation in milk procurement prices exerted meaningful pressure on margins and heightened competitive intensity in certain markets weighed on financial performance. Mitigation is via cost control, operating efficiencies, portfolio optimisation and a brand-led / value-added strategy, but recovery is explicitly conditioned on input cost pressures moderating.
- Feed cost volatility and pricing pressure in Poultry & Processed Foods — The business operates in a dynamic environment characterised by feed cost volatility and pricing pressures; profitability remained influenced by fluctuations in input costs and competitive intensity. Margin improvement is dependent on input cost volatility moderating and operating leverage improving.
- Pan-India operating exposure to economic, regulatory and political conditions and competitor actions — The Board's Report states the Company has substantial operations spread almost all over the country and its competitive position is influenced by economic, regulatory and political situations and the actions of competitors. The Board, supported by the Audit Committee, reviews the effectiveness of the risk management process covering all material risks; the Board's stated opinion is that no risks have been identified which may threaten the existence of the Company. Risk Management Committee met twice in FY 2025-26 (August 6, 2025 and February 3, 2026).

business.body: Godrej Agrovet makes and sells animal nutrition products (cattle feed, layer feed, aqua feed and specialty nutrition), crop protection products (in-house differentiated herbicide and insecticide formulations plus selectively in-licensed products) and oil palm products (crude palm oil, palm kernel oil and allied products processed from Fresh Fruit Bunches), selling primarily to Indian farmers through deep on-ground farmer engagement, field demonstrations and advisory networks. Through its subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates the Company also has interests in dairy products, poultry, value-added vegetarian and non-vegetarian products, cattle breeding and dairy farming, and — via Astec LifeSciences — agrochemical active ingredients (technical), bulk and formulations and intermediate products, including a contract development and manufacturing (CDMO) business. Its footprint extends beyond India through the ACI Godrej Agrovet joint venture in Bangladesh, Astec's exports to approximately 17 countries, and an Astec subsidiary in Bogota, Colombia.

outlook.body:
- Pivot the portfolio towards more value-added, branded and higher-margin revenue streams across all business segments, anchored in a long-term vision of building a sustainable, growth-oriented and profitable agri-business value chain.
- Treat R&D as a key pillar of long-term growth and sharpen the R&D focus to be deeply consumer-centric, identifying emerging need gaps and unmet expectations to accelerate differentiated product innovation across Animal Nutrition, Crop Care, Astec and Oil Palm.
- Run an enterprise-wide digital transformation: SAP S/4HANA (Wave 1 gone live, Wave 2 in progress) plus continued investment in digital platforms, farmer engagement platforms, AI-enabled tools and data-driven decision-making.
- Crop Care: execute on differentiated in-house formulations, selective in-licensing and customer-centric demand generation, and broaden crop coverage beyond traditional focus areas into crops such as maize and paddy to reduce dependence on a limited set of crops.
- Astec LifeSciences: accelerate the CDMO business as a key strategic priority, leveraging the 'Adi Godrej Centre for Chemical Research and Development' to deepen customer partnerships, support R&D-led scale-up and expand the pipeline of complex and differentiated molecules, while pursuing select high-margin opportunities in the enterprise portfolio.
- Oil Palm: continue investments in area expansion, farmer partnerships and downstream integration, supported by plantation development, nursery operations, scientific agronomy and expansion of the Samadhan Center farmer-engagement network.
- Godrej Foods: continue the strategic transformation towards a higher share of branded and value-added products, building consumer franchises while reducing dependence on volatile categories.
- Dairy: focus on operational efficiencies, portfolio optimization and strengthening the value-added products portfolio through targeted innovation and consumer-centric offerings.
- Sustain capital efficiency through disciplined credit management, accelerated collections and inventory optimization to keep net working capital and ROCE improving, strengthening the ability to invest for the future.
- Embed sustainability via the Godrej Industries Group 'Good & Green' vision — climate action, water stewardship, farmer prosperity, responsible sourcing and sustainable innovation — including science-based emission reduction targets aligned to the 'Well Below 2°C' scenario.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY 2025-26 expansion activity at Godrej Agrovet was concentrated in Oil Palm value-chain investment, a feed-plant product conversion and better utilisation of subsidiary capacity, rather than in any newly announced greenfield plant with a commissioning date. In Vegetable Oil, the Directors' Report describes the year's performance as underpinned by "sustained investments across the value chain, including plantation development, nursery operations and deep farmer engagement, with continued focus on scientific agronomy, productivity enhancement and process efficiencies improving yields and mill performance"; the Chairman adds that "continued investments in area expansion, farmer partnerships, and downstream integration have further strengthened our leadership position". The farmer-facing footprint was widened through "the expansion of the Samadhan Center network to 24 Centers during the year". In Animal Nutrition, "Aqua feed production has successfully commenced at the Bani unit, originally designed for poultry feed manufacturing" — the switch was achieved by leveraging the existing layout and infrastructure through in-house process optimisation, parameter tuning and Kaizens, with "Plant utilization increased by up to 14%" and savings of approximately Rs 70 lakh in FY 2025-26. Supporting plant-level technology work during the year included an automatic water recovery system in the boiler circuit (recovery and reuse of more than 750 KL of water per month), temperature sensors and alarm systems on the Crumblers for product-quality control, and implementation of the YKL Press to recover residual oil from Empty Fruit Bunches while lowering their moisture so the processed EFB can be used as boiler fuel (cost savings of approximately Rs 95 lakh). An imported pulverizer installed at a plant for fine grinding of raw material for producing aquaculture feeds (year of import 2023-24) is reported as fully absorbed. The Company states that "the capital expenditure on specific technologies to improve the environmental and social impacts of products and processes made by your Company during the Financial Year 2025-26 was Rs 4.53 Crore". At subsidiary Astec LifeSciences, the turnaround to EBITDA break-even was attributed to higher volumes across the enterprise and CDMO portfolios with "enhanced capacity utilization compared to the previous year", and the parent raised its holding from 64.75% to 67.03% by subscribing to Astec's Rights Issue. In Crop Care, expansion was product/crop-led rather than asset-led: new herbicide and insecticide launches (Ashitaka in maize, Takai in paddy) marked "a strategic broadening of crop coverage beyond traditional focus areas". The routed text contains no installed-capacity table, no named plant commissioning or ramp-up timeline, and no forward capex programme or budget.

outlook.body:
- India's real GDP growth for FY 2025-26 estimated at 7.6 percent versus 7.1 percent in FY25 (RBI annual report), with the IMF's April 2026 World Economic Outlook projecting 6.5 percent for both FY27 and FY28 — India retaining its position as the fastest-growing major economy.
- Agriculture and allied sector as a stable anchor: real GVA from agriculture and allied activities estimated to grow ~3.1% in FY 2025-26, with moderation attributed to muted food price inflation rather than a decline in physical output.
- Strong rural demand indicators — adequate monsoon, healthy reservoir levels, and tractor sales (a key proxy for rural sentiment) up 19 percent in FY26 crossing one million units, reflecting improved farm liquidity and mechanisation.
- Key near-term monitorable: the initial long-range forecast for the 2026 southwest monsoon indicates a below-normal rainfall outlook, raising downside risks to kharif sowing and rural sentiment.
- Supportive policy backdrop from Union Budget 2026-27 — transition from subsistence to high-value market-linked agri-food systems, integrated development of 500 reservoirs and Amrit Sarovars, high-value crop programmes, fisheries value-chain support, a loan-linked capital subsidy scheme in animal husbandry, and the Bharat VISTAAR AI-enabled advisory platform — expected to create scalable growth opportunities across the value chain for integrated agri-business groups.
- Structural transformation of Indian agriculture through precision agriculture, IoT sensors, drones, satellite crop monitoring, AI-driven advisory and digital supply chains, plus growth in agri-tech, agri-fintech and organised agri-logistics.
- Animal Nutrition: volume-led growth across cattle, layer, aqua and specialty feed driven by deep farmer engagement, strong brand equity and improving product mix; profitability aided by moderation in key raw material prices, better product mix and continued operational efficiencies.
- ACI GAVL (Bangladesh JV): with the conclusion of elections the operating environment is expected to normalize, providing greater stability and improved visibility; long-term outlook positive on structural growth in the livestock sector, increasing formalization of feed consumption and rising acceptance of high-quality performance-oriented nutrition solutions.
- Crop Care: near-term demand impacted by adverse weather, acreage shifts and heightened competitive and regulatory intensity in cotton, chilies and grapes; recovery expected to be driven by innovation-led portfolio expansion, increased R&D investment, strategic collaborations and deeper penetration across a wider range of crops and use-cases.
- Astec LifeSciences: turnaround supported by higher volumes across enterprise and CDMO portfolios, improved realizations, better demand conditions, enhanced capacity utilization, normalization of channel inventories and improved operating leverage — positioning the company for sustained recovery.
- Oil Palm: higher Fresh Fruit Bunch arrivals, sustained improvement in oil extraction ratio, effective cost management and supportive realizations for crude palm oil and palm kernel oil driving revenue and profitability.
- Dairy: headwinds from elevated milk procurement costs and temporary demand disruption caused by unseasonal rainfall in the first half of the financial year.
- External risk overlay: the ongoing West Asia conflict introduces risks through energy prices, shipping costs and financial market volatility; as a large net importer of crude oil India remains exposed to supply disruptions and price spikes, though strong domestic demand provides a counterbalance. The World Bank projects a slowdown in global growth (~2.5%).
- Astec LifeSciences intends to expand its pipeline of complex and differentiated molecules in the CDMO business, leveraging the Adi Godrej Centre for Chemical Research and Development to deepen customer partnerships and support R&D-led scale-up (qualitative pipeline reference; no order-book value disclosed).
- Animal Nutrition strengthened its innovation pipeline during the year with the launch of Dhanalaxmi G (premium cattle feed for high-yielding cows and buffaloes) and Bypro Plus (enhanced protein formulation), both seeing encouraging early adoption in initial launch markets.

deepdive.thesis: GAVL crossed INR 10,000 Cr revenue with 9% growth driven by volume-led expansion in Animal Nutrition and Oil Palm, while Crop Care faces a temporary inventory overhang before a projected H2 recovery. The strategic pivot to high-value segments (branded foods, specialty agrochemicals) and Astec's EBITDA breakeven mark a inflection in earnings quality, supported by a 'demographic dividend' in oil palm plantations offsetting near-term monsoon risks.

open.item: PKO refinery to come into production in Q3FY26.
Deep portfolio strategy work at fag end; clear sharp choices on priority vs de-priority businesses and capital allocation to be communicated to the Street around early April 2026.
Astec EBITDA break-even guidance for FY26 reiterated; turnaround 'well and truly in play'.
New CPO processing plant in Khammam to go live within ~2 months (by ~Q4FY26).
Oil palm acreage expansion of ~17,000-18,000 hectares for FY26 (15,000 done in 9M, ~2x last year).
Q4FY26 Crop Protection to be hit by a one-time base effect from prior-year Hitweed co-marketing sales; ex-that, healthy top-line growth targeted.
Astec to deliver ~20% revenue growth in FY26 with positive EBITDA (EBITDA break-even) for the year.
Astec rights issue proceeds to be used to repay debts in the books.
Dairy EBITDA margin (excluding working media) of 5.5-6% for full-year FY26 (6-7% including working media), with 1-1.5% improvement aimed over time.
Interesterification and hydrogenation to start in Q4FY26, enabling bakery fat, shortening and other value-added products.
Oil palm FFB arrivals to grow 15-18% over FY25 (Q1 already +52%), OER better than last year.
Astec CDMO and new products to reach over Rs 300 crore in FY26, about 65% of total sales.
Astec expected to report EBITDA break-even for FY26, targeting turnover of Rs 500 crore.
Crop Protection EBIT margin to be maintained around 28-30% in FY26 (last year's 40%+ was an outlier).
GAVL top-line growth maintained in the early teens for FY26 (revised from earlier 16-18%), with profit expectation maintained.
Astec loss to come down to less than half of last year's (~Rs 140 crore loss in FY25); EBITDA positive but still PAT loss-making.
Animal Feed EBIT per ton to average Rs 1,900-2,000 across FY26.
Astec contract manufacturing/CDMO to grow ~35% year-on-year for the next couple of years, mostly from old molecules ramping.
GAVL consolidated bottom-line to grow 16-18% in FY26, mostly from loss reduction in Astec.
GAVL consolidated top-line to grow 16-18% in FY26, driven only by volume (not inflation).
